Headed back to DC early and already the madness has begun. First stop—a rally standing in solidarity with Tribal Leaders opposing a permitting deal scheduled for a vote in the Senate TODAY at 5:30 PM.

This is a bill that has had no public process, no hearings, and which Trump bragged himself last night he’d use to push through pipelines and data centers. Especially in light of last week’s historic election, we’re asking the Senate to take a beat. Here’s why ⬇️

This bill is a Trojan Horse.

Why would anyone vote for this permitting bill after voters have just handed us the largest midterm repudiation of a sitting President in American history?

I urge my Senate colleagues to vote NO.

We cannot greenlight transmission at any cost, including undermining tribal sovereignty, protections for sacred sites, public lands, clean water, wildlife, and the environment for generations to come. We can, and we must, pass a bill we can actually believe in—not a false promise.

We love our Land Grants! From Chilili, to Carnuel, Tajique and Torreón to Tomé, Anton Chico to Las Huertas and Manzano—New Mexico’s land grants are the keepers of generations of tradition, stewardship, and connection to the places that have sustained families for centuries.

Every day, we’re proud and grateful to work alongside our Land Grants to honor that history and protect the lands, waters, and traditions of our Land Grant-Mercedes; to work alongside @RepTeresaLF and @SenatorLujan to protect traditional uses and land stewardship; and to invest in acequias and bring home funding for vital infrastructure. 

Our land grants are more than a part of New Mexico’s history. They are a part of who we are as a state. Which is why when I took my oath of office, I was sworn in on both the Constitution AND the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo! Because, our job is to ensure we are fighting every day to protect the rights of our people and the communities that make New Mexico who we are, for generations to come!

To all of our friends in the Four Corners being impacted by these floods please stay safe, follow evacuation orders, and take care!

As someone who was born in Farmington, just one block from the San Juan River, my heart is breaking to see the flooding in so many of our communities. 

Our office is standing alongside Congresswoman @RepTeresaLF and the entire New Mexico delegation to help! 💔

In New Mexico, water is life. And I have spent my entire career dedicated to working on water, conservation, and community development.

That’s why, as your Congresswoman, I have fought to protect our lands and waters, to pass legislation protecting the sacred sites and water rights of Tribes and Pueblos, and to protect Chaco Canyon, the Buffalo Tract, Mt. Taylor, Bears Ears, and Oak Flat. It’s why I passed the NM Water Data Act and Grid Modernization bill and have brought home millions for water infrastructure, including for our irrigation, acequia, drinking water, and wastewater systems.

And it’s why, as a member of the Natural Resources Committee, I’m fighting on the front lines to protect our lands, our waters, our clean air, and our wildlife, and fighting for climate action every day! This is our fight for New Mexico and for our planet. 🌎❤️💕

We’re here to stand with survivors! Days ago a colleague was violently sexually assaulted in Phoenix. As a member of the Democratic Women’s Caucus @DemWomenCaucus we’re here to stand with Bernadette Greene-Placentia and all survivors.

That’s why I’ve brought home millions for seniors, veterans, affordable housing, health clinics, food programs, and more to help our communities.  

Because, we see you, we hear you, and know our communities are struggling. And, that is why we are fighting every day to make sure every New Mexican can live with joy, dignity, and purpose! ❤️

Healthcare is a human right!

That’s why I’ve brought home millions for local hospitals and clinics, to build and expand behavioral health clinics, and for emergency services across the state. From Bernalillo to Belen, Ft. Sumner to Sandia—these facilities will help save lives. 

It’s why I’ve also fought to protect Medicare and Medicaid from disastrous cuts, expand rural clinics, and invest in the pipeline for new nurses, doctors and healthcare workers. It’s why I helped pass the PACT Act to expand care for veterans and legislation to protect maternal health and lower prescription drug prices, and expand access in Tribal communities.

We’re not going to stop fighting for the care New Mexicans deserve. ❤️

Happy Indigenous Peoples’ Day! ❤️

Today and every day we celebrate the leadership, resilience, history, cultures, languages, and accomplishments of Tribal communities here in New Mexico and all across the country. 

Every day we are honored to work alongside Tribal and Pueblo leaders to keep doing the work—whether that’s fighting to protect sacred lands and waters, investing in housing, schools, clinics, and economic opportunities, honoring our veterans, and celebrating the people in our communities. We are building New Mexico and our economy!

We know New Mexicans are strong and resilient, but struggling to get by—and that is why EVERY DAY we’re fighting to address the costs of housing, food, other essentials and to rebuild our economy—because every New Mexican should be able to put food on the table, a roof over their head, and live with dignity and purpose!

Over the last 5 years, we’ve worked tirelessly to bring home millions for economic development, infrastructure, and good union jobs. I’ve helped support schools, clinics, and trades programs and secured millions for housing, food assistance, and other programs that help New Mexico families thrive—while fighting to build jobs, protect Social Security, expand healthcare, and build a brighter future for our state. 

Because—this is the work we love to do and as New Mexicans, we take care of each other!

roll_calls.plain_language: Official question: On Passage. H.R. 2102: Major Richard Star Act. Result: Passed.

post.text:
In New Mexico, service is a way of life. Every day we are deeply grateful for our Service Members, their families, and all of our veterans across the state. 

From Kirtland Air Force Base, to our National Guard, to every veteran in every community across New Mexico—we are working every day to support those who have worn the uniform and to invest in critical infrastructure, benefits, and care. 

I am proud to co-sponsor the Major Richard Star Act for combat veterans, to have helped pass the PACT Act, secured vital funding to build ABQ’s first Veterans Integration Center for homeless vets, and to be fighting to protect and expand access to care and benefits every day! Thank you to all who serve. 🇺🇸❤️🤍💙
